# Heatmaps {.divider}

[Expression matrices · Day 01]{.eyebrow}


<!-- slide 169 -->
## What a Heatmap Shows {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps · theory]{.eyebrow}

### Colour, clustering, annotation

A heatmap turns a matrix into a grid of coloured cells: gene × sample expression, a sample-by-sample correlation matrix, an epigenomic signal. Colour encodes the value, so the choice of map matters, **diverging** (e.g. `RdBu_r`, centred at 0) for z-scores that go both ways, sequential for one-directional quantities.

Two moves make it readable. **Z-score each gene** so a quietly-expressed gene and a loud one are on the same scale (colour then means "high/low *for this gene*"). Then **cluster** rows and columns so similar genes and similar samples sit together, the dendrograms reorder the matrix until the structure appears. `seaborn.clustermap` does both with good defaults; `PyComplexHeatmap` adds rich annotation tracks.


<!-- slide 170 -->
## Heatmap · The Data {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps]{.eyebrow}

### A real expression matrix + its sample metadata

`load_expression()` is a log2 matrix, genes down the rows, samples across the columns. `load_expression_meta()` is the matching per-sample table (condition, batch, QC), the annotation we'll layer on top.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
from genomics_course.data import load_expression, load_expression_meta

expr = load_expression()        # 40 genes × 24 samples
meta = load_expression_meta()   # sample, condition, batch, qc
expr.iloc[:3, :4]
```


<!-- slide 171 -->
## Heatmap · Step 1 — Z-Score & Colour {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps · build]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · Put every gene on one scale

Z-score each gene (row), so colour means high or low *relative to that gene's own mean*. Drop it into `sns.heatmap` with a diverging map centred at 0. The blocks are faintly there, but the rows and columns are still in file order.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "5,8-10"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.0
#| fig-height: 5.0
import seaborn as sns                                       # heatmap / clustermap library
from genomics_course.data import load_expression

expr = load_expression()                                    # genes × samples (log2)
z = expr.sub(expr.mean(1), axis=0).div(expr.std(1), axis=0) # z-score each gene: mean 0, sd 1

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.0, 5.0))                  # one panel
sns.heatmap(z, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, ax=ax,              # diverging map, white at z = 0
            cbar_kws={"label": "z-score"},                  # colourbar legend
            xticklabels=False, yticklabels=False)           # 40×24 labels would be unreadable
ax.set_xlabel("samples"); ax.set_ylabel("genes")
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 172 -->
## Heatmap · Step 2 — Cluster It {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps · build]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · Let the structure sort itself

Swap `heatmap` for `clustermap`. It hierarchically clusters rows and columns and reorders both, adding dendrograms. Similar genes pull together, similar samples pull together, and the two modules and two conditions snap into clean blocks.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "7-9"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.0
#| fig-height: 5.5
import seaborn as sns
from genomics_course.data import load_expression

expr = load_expression()                                    # genes × samples
z = expr.sub(expr.mean(1), axis=0).div(expr.std(1), axis=0) # per-gene z-score

cg = sns.clustermap(z, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0,             # cluster rows AND columns
                    figsize=(6.0, 5.5), xticklabels=False, yticklabels=False,
                    cbar_kws={"label": "z-score"})          # dendrograms added automatically
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 173 -->
## Heatmap · Step 3 — Annotate the Samples {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps · build]{.eyebrow}

### 3 · Bring in the metadata

Map each sample's condition to a colour and pass it as `col_colors`. A strip appears above the columns, so you can check that the clusters actually recover the biology, not a batch artefact.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "8-9,12"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.0
#| fig-height: 5.5
import seaborn as sns
from genomics_course.data import load_expression, load_expression_meta

expr = load_expression()                                    # genes × samples
meta = load_expression_meta()                               # sample, condition, batch, qc
z = expr.sub(expr.mean(1), axis=0).div(expr.std(1), axis=0) # per-gene z-score

cond_pal = {"Control": BLUE, "Drought": AMBER}              # one colour per condition
col_colors = meta.set_index("sample")["condition"].map(cond_pal)  # colour for each sample column

cg = sns.clustermap(z, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, figsize=(6.0, 5.5),
                    col_colors=col_colors,                  # condition strip above the columns
                    xticklabels=False, yticklabels=False, cbar_kws={"label": "z-score"})
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 174 -->
## Heatmap · Step 4 — Polish & Title {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps · build]{.eyebrow}

### 4 · Slim the trees, add a key, name the finding

Thin the dendrograms, mute their colour, add a legend for the annotation strip, and title with the result. The figure now reads itself: two gene modules, cleanly split by condition.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "2,15-20"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.0
#| fig-height: 5.5
import seaborn as sns
from matplotlib.patches import Patch                        # to build the condition legend
from genomics_course.data import load_expression, load_expression_meta

expr = load_expression()                                    # genes × samples
meta = load_expression_meta()                               # metadata
z = expr.sub(expr.mean(1), axis=0).div(expr.std(1), axis=0) # per-gene z-score

cond_pal = {"Control": BLUE, "Drought": AMBER}              # condition colours
col_colors = meta.set_index("sample")["condition"].map(cond_pal)  # per-column colour

cg = sns.clustermap(z, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, figsize=(6.0, 5.5),
                    col_colors=col_colors, xticklabels=False, yticklabels=False,
                    cbar_kws={"label": "z-score"},
                    dendrogram_ratio=(.12, .12),            # slimmer dendrograms
                    tree_kws={"colors": MUTED, "linewidths": .6})  # muted tree lines
handles = [Patch(color=c, label=k) for k, c in cond_pal.items()]   # legend swatches
cg.ax_col_dendrogram.legend(handles=handles, ncol=2,        # put the key over the top dendrogram
                            frameon=False, loc="center", fontsize=8)
cg.fig.suptitle("Drought genes split into two modules",     # title states the finding
                fontweight="bold", color=INK, y=1.02)
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
[The bottom line]{.tl}
The recipe: **z-score each gene → cluster rows and columns → annotate the samples → title the finding**. Z-scoring makes genes comparable; clustering reorders the matrix until structure appears; the annotation strip proves the clusters are biology, not batch.
:::


<!-- slide 175 -->
## Level Up · PyComplexHeatmap {.smaller .scrollable}

[Expression heatmaps · advanced]{.eyebrow}

### Several annotation tracks at once

For publication figures with stacked tracks (categorical strips + numeric mini-barplots), `PyComplexHeatmap` mirrors R's ComplexHeatmap. One `HeatmapAnnotation` holds every track.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# pip install PyComplexHeatmap
from PyComplexHeatmap import HeatmapAnnotation, anno_simple, anno_barplot, ClusterMapPlotter
from genomics_course.data import load_expression, load_expression_meta

expr = load_expression()
meta = load_expression_meta().set_index("sample")           # align metadata to matrix columns
z = expr.sub(expr.mean(1), axis=0).div(expr.std(1), axis=0) # per-gene z-score

col_ha = HeatmapAnnotation(                                 # one object, several stacked tracks
    Condition=anno_simple(meta["condition"],                # categorical strip
                          colors={"Control": BLUE, "Drought": AMBER}),
    Batch=anno_simple(meta["batch"]),                       # second categorical strip
    QC=anno_barplot(meta["qc"], colors=GREEN, height=12),   # numeric mini-barplot
    axis=1, verbose=0)

ClusterMapPlotter(data=z, top_annotation=col_ha, cmap="RdBu_r",  # clustered heatmap + tracks
                  row_cluster=True, col_cluster=True, label="z-score",
                  show_rownames=False, show_colnames=False)
```

## Exercise · Sample QC {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps · exercise]{.eyebrow}

### Did the replicates behave?

::: {.exercise}
[Real scenario]{.xl}
Before trusting any analysis, check that replicates agree and nothing is mislabelled. Build a **sample × sample correlation heatmap**, annotate it by condition, and read whether the two groups form clean blocks, or whether a sample sits in the wrong one (a possible swap).

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
import seaborn as sns
from genomics_course.data import load_expression, load_expression_meta

expr = load_expression()
meta = load_expression_meta()

# 1. corr = expr.corr()                                    # sample × sample Pearson matrix
# 2. col  = meta.set_index("sample")["condition"].map({"Control": BLUE, "Drought": AMBER})
# 3. sns.clustermap(corr, cmap="rocket", row_colors=col, col_colors=col)
# 4. read it: two clean blocks? any sample correlating with the wrong group?
```
:::


<!-- slide 177 -->
## Exercise · Top Variable Genes {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps · exercise]{.eyebrow}

### You can't cluster 20,000 genes

::: {.exercise}
[Real scenario]{.xl}
The standard first look at an RNA-seq matrix isn't every gene, it's the most *variable* ones, the genes carrying the signal. Select the top 20 by row variance and cluster just those.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
import seaborn as sns
from genomics_course.data import load_expression

expr = load_expression()
z = expr.sub(expr.mean(1), axis=0).div(expr.std(1), axis=0)

# 1. top = z.var(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).head(20).index   # 20 most variable genes
# 2. sns.clustermap(z.loc[top], cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, yticklabels=True)
# 3. do the same two modules still separate the conditions with only 20 genes?
```
:::
